headline: Ideas into
intro: I’m Keira Haugh, a graphic design and communications student. My work spans visual identity, typography and digital design.
about: I’m a graphic design and communications student with a particular interest in how people find their way through apps and websites. My projects range from building a typeface out of repeating lines to designing a walking app with a group of other students.
opportunities: I’d love to hear about graphic design projects, digital design opportunities and collaborations.
skills: Adobe Creative Cloud, Figma and Canva
interests: Reading, writing, music and gaming are a big part of where I find inspiration. I’m also drawn to thoughtful UX and UI design, especially the choices that make an app or website feel intuitive to use.

projects.title: Hawksans Typeface
projects.description: An elongated modular display face, explored through a printed specimen.
projects.brief: Explore how far a sans serif letterform can stretch while remaining readable. I developed Hawksans as a modular display face for large-scale use.
projects.process: I used grids and repeated strokes to construct the letters, adjusting their proportions and spacing to find a rhythm across the alphabet.
projects.decisions: Long vertical strokes create the optical effect. In the specimen, a repeated pattern on black faces two isolated letters on burgundy, so the reader can see both the texture and the construction.
projects.outcome: Making the specimen deepened my understanding of type anatomy and optical balance, especially how small changes in spacing affect a distorted letter.
projects.alt: Black, white and burgundy type specimen featuring narrow modular letterforms.

gallery.alt: Flat specimen showing repeated linear glyphs beside two enlarged letters.
gallery.caption: Isolating two letters reveals the narrow gaps between their strokes.

gallery.alt: A burgundy specimen cover with white linear type on an ochre chair.
gallery.caption: The cover uses the letterforms at display scale.

gallery.alt: Open printed spread about modular typography.
gallery.caption: A quieter text spread gives the reader a break from the dense display lettering.

projects.title: Pilcrow
projects.description: A Figma website for a fictional creative collective to share artists’ work.
projects.brief: Design a website for Pilcrow, a fictional creative collective, to showcase artists’ work and highlight member contributions.
projects.process: I designed the collective’s website in Figma, organising projects, interviews and member features into repeatable layouts.
projects.decisions: A recurring wavy line connects the pages. Muted surfaces leave room for the artists’ colours, and a modular grid carries the content from desktop to mobile.
projects.outcome: The final designs show how a visitor moves from the collective’s homepage to individual projects and interviews.
projects.alt: Two Pilcrow website screens suspended against a pale mint background.

gallery.alt: Two phones showing Pilcrow’s homepage and interview layout.
gallery.caption: The modular project grid becomes a compact mobile layout. The wavy border carries through to the interview.

gallery.alt: A series of Pilcrow page designs showing artwork, features and member profiles.

projects.title: Pause The Noise
projects.description: A poster campaign and digital layouts built around the message “Break the cycle”.
projects.brief: For a citizen design brief, I chose headline fatigue and doomscrolling. The campaign invites people to take a break from the stream of news on their phones.
projects.process: I developed contrasting poster versions and designed a companion website mock-up in Figma. A QR code on each poster connects the printed campaign to the digital resource.
projects.decisions: Oversized words sit behind the phone users’ silhouettes. Pink speech panels interrupt the monochrome composition, drawing attention to the campaign’s message.
projects.outcome: The final series pairs street posters with a digital guide to taking a break from scrolling.
projects.alt: Two contrasting Pause The Noise posters mounted in an ivy-covered wall.

gallery.alt: Detail of the light poster with silhouette and pink speech panels.
gallery.caption: The silhouette cuts across the headline, while the pink panels remain distinct from both.

gallery.alt: Four alternating light and dark campaign posters on a street frontage.
gallery.caption: Reversing the tones gives the posters a rhythm when displayed in sequence.

gallery.alt: Three campaign page layouts combining photography, text and green accents.

projects.title: Wandr
projects.description: A group project imagining Limerick’s cultural life as a walkable digital archive.
projects.brief: As a group, we imagined how people in 2050 might explore Limerick’s street art, fashion and independent businesses as they existed in 2026.
projects.process: We gathered different perspectives on the city and translated them into mapped walks, notifications and augmented reality overlays.
projects.decisions: Bold headings echo street signage. A pale map keeps the streets legible, while purple identifies routes and controls. Notifications let walkers look up from the screen.
projects.outcome: The concept follows a walker from choosing a route through to a summary of the places they discovered.
projects.alt: Wandr route summary and Limerick street art walk displayed on two phones.

gallery.alt: Type, purple colour swatches and navigation components from the Wandr design system.
gallery.caption: A shared set of type styles and components brings the different walking screens together.

gallery.alt: Wandr screen offering an augmented reality view.

projects.title: Between The Lines
projects.description: Layered handwriting and distorted letterforms meet in a monochrome street poster.
projects.brief: Create a typographic response to Between Us — Contemporary Irish Fiction, a Cúirt event featuring Sally Rooney, Donal Ryan and Megan Nolan. I focused on feelings that remain unspoken.
projects.process: I used fragments of text about unanswered questions and being alone to guide the line breaks, spacing and disrupted alignments.
projects.decisions: Uneven spacing makes the letters seem to move forward and pull back. A single orange mark punctuates the muted composition, while clear event lettering gives the reader a point of entry.
projects.outcome: The visual response extends from street posters to mobile event graphics.
projects.alt: A grey framed street poster with warped white lettering and an orange dot.

gallery.alt: Close-up of disrupted white type, handwriting and an orange dot.
gallery.caption: The interrupted letterforms echo thoughts that never quite become speech.

gallery.alt: The Between Us poster shown on two faces of a street display.
gallery.caption: The diagonal event title sits below the experimental lettering.

gallery.alt: Two mobile graphics for Between Us and the Cúirt festival.
gallery.caption: The handwritten texture connects the event poster to the mobile graphics.

projects.title: Pery’s Bingo
projects.description: Event posters, social campaigns and a weekly schedule from my placement at Parnell Plaza.
projects.brief: During my six-week placement at Parnell Plaza in Limerick, I designed graphics for Pery’s Bingo events in the hall and online. Each piece needed to communicate dates, times and offers at a glance.
projects.process: I learned Canva alongside my existing Adobe skills and used Facebook and website analytics to understand what regular players responded to. I proposed bringing the weekly events together on one poster.
projects.decisions: Each day has a name, colour and calendar icon. For seasonal campaigns, I paired a simple announcement with a separate information graphic, keeping the type, illustration and palette consistent across both.
projects.outcome: The weekly schedule was used in the hall and on social media. It became the standard format for communicating the venue’s 2026 weekly programme.
projects.alt: Pery’s Bingo weekly schedule with five colour-coded event panels and calendar icons.

projects.title: 18 Grams
projects.description: An artisan coffee identity built around the precision of a single measure.
projects.brief: The brief was to create a brand identity for an artisan coffee shop. The name 18 Grams connects the idea of precision with speciality coffee.
projects.decisions: The fine-line coffee tool sits alongside the wordmark on an apron. The menu carries the same restrained lettering onto a warm, pale surface.
projects.alt: The 18 Grams wordmark and portafilter symbol printed on a taupe apron.

gallery.alt: Detail of the fine-line portafilter and 18 Grams lettering on the apron.
gallery.caption: The handle of the portafilter follows the horizontal line of the wordmark.

gallery.alt: An 18 Grams menu mounted on a wooden board.

projects.title: Fleeting Moments
projects.description: A photographic mosaic and a figure on a bench, framed in the light of a bus shelter.
projects.decisions: A shift from amber to deep brown anchors the figure at the bottom of the image. Pale italic lettering crosses the mosaic in two staggered lines.
projects.alt: A golden Fleeting Moments poster in a sunlit outdoor display.

gallery.alt: Detail of small image tiles beneath the Fleeting Moments title.
gallery.caption: Up close, the amber field resolves into individual images.
